proof_summary: For an even integer \(m=2N\), a witness at the midpoint \(N\) supplies primes \(N-k\) and \(N+k\), whose sum is \(m\); the finitely many cases \(2\le N\le6\) are handled directly. For odd \(n>7\), applying the hypothesis to the even number \(n-1\) gives a prime \(p\) and the prime \((n-1)-(2p-1)=n-2p\), hence \(n=(n-2p)+2p\), with \(n=7\) handled separately.
